title: Climb by the next number's factor
W: Halve even numbers. For odd n, add the largest prime factor of n + 1. Every tested start ends in the loop through 1 or the loop 7 → 9 → 14 → 7. Prove it.
M: Let $g(n)=n/2$ ($n$ even), $n+P(n+1)$ ($n$ odd). Prove every orbit enters $(1,3,5,8,4,2)$ or $(7,9,14)$.

title: P(n)+P(n+1)−1
W: Replace n by P(n) + P(n + 1) − 1. Every tested start ends in one of three loops. Prove these are the only ones.
M: Prove every orbit of $n\mapsto P(n)+P(n+1)-1$ on $n\ge2$ enters $(4,6,9,7,8)$, $(17,19,23,25)$ or $(167,173,201)$.

title: Neighbours' largest factors
W: Replace n by P(n − 1) + P(n + 1). Every tested start ends at 5 or in one of three loops, of lengths 11, 18 and 4. Prove there is nothing else.
M: Prove every orbit of $n\mapsto P(n-1)+P(n+1)$ on $n\ge3$ enters $\{5\}$, the 11-cycle through 8, the 18-cycle through 24, or $(224,228,456,470)$.

title: Last digits of consecutive largest factors
W: Look at the last digits of P(n) and P(n + 1). Show the 16 possible pairs of last digits from {1, 3, 7, 9} occur equally often.
M: Prove $\#\{n\le x: P(n)\equiv a,\ P(n+1)\equiv b\ (10)\}\sim\frac{x}{16}$ for all $a,b\in\{1,3,7,9\}$.

title: Prime continued fractions
W: Consider real numbers whose continued fraction terms are all prime. Show the fractal dimension of this set is transcendental.
M: Let $E=\{x\in(0,1): \text{all partial quotients of }x\text{ are prime}\}$. Prove $\dim_H E$ is transcendental.

title: Prime plus two seven-free squares
W: Show every large number is a prime plus a sum of two squares whose bases have no digit 7.
M: Prove every sufficiently large $n$ is $p+a^2+b^2$ with $p$ prime and $a,b$ free of the decimal digit 7.

title: Infinite monochromatic square-sum paths
W: Colour the positive integers red and blue. Show there is always an infinite increasing sequence of one colour in which every two consecutive terms sum to a perfect square.
M: Prove every 2-colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ admits $a_1<a_2<\cdots$ of one colour with $a_i+a_{i+1}$ a perfect square for all $i$.

title: Roth for seven-free numbers
W: Show every subset of the seven-free numbers that keeps a fixed fraction of them contains three in arithmetic progression.
M: Prove for every $\delta>0$ and large $N$, every $A\subseteq\{n\le N:7\notin n\}$ with $|A|\ge\delta\#\{n\le N:7\notin n\}$ contains a nontrivial 3-term AP.

title: Partizan Prime Nim
W: Left may remove a prime that is 1 mod 4, Right a prime that is 3 mod 4, from one pile. Describe the game values.
M: For the partizan subtraction game with $L=\{p\equiv1\ (4)\}$, $R=\{p\equiv3\ (4)\}$, prove every position is equal to a number or a number plus a switch of bounded temperature, and find the bound.

title: Is Prime Nim's losing set definable?
W: Add the set of Prime Nim losing positions to the arithmetic of addition. Is the resulting theory decidable?
M: Decide whether the first-order theory of $(\mathbb{N},+,L)$ is decidable, where $L=\{n:G(n)=0\}$ for the prime subtraction game.

title: Hamiltonian induced subgraphs of S_N
W: Show deciding whether a given set of numbers can be lined up so neighbours sum to squares is NP-complete.
M: Prove NP-completeness of: given $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ (in binary), decide whether $S_\infty[A]$ has a Hamiltonian path.

title: Fibonacci-sum chains
W: Join two numbers if their sum is a Fibonacci number. Decide for which N the numbers 1 to N can be lined up with neighbours always joined.
M: Let $F_N$ join $a\ne b\in[N]$ when $a+b$ is a Fibonacci number. Determine all $N$ for which $F_N$ has a Hamiltonian path.

title: Ramsey for prime sums of three
W: Colour the integers with two colours. Show there are always three distinct numbers of one colour whose three pairwise sums are all prime, or a forced obstruction to this.
M: Decide whether every 2-colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ contains distinct $a,b,c$ of one colour with $a+b,a+c,b+c$ all prime.

title: Graceful square-sum paths
W: Find infinitely many N for which 1 to N can be lined up with neighbours summing to squares and with all neighbour differences distinct.
M: Prove infinitely many $N$ admit a Hamiltonian path $v_1\dots v_N$ of $S_N$ with $|v_{i+1}-v_i|$ pairwise distinct.

title: Prime-sum graph is Hamiltonian-connected
W: Show you can line up 1 to 2n with neighbours summing to primes, starting with any odd number and ending with any even one.
M: Prove for all large $n$ and all odd $a$, even $b$ in $[2n]$, the prime-sum graph on $[2n]$ has a Hamiltonian $a$–$b$ path.

title: No long climbs for 2P(n)+1
W: Show the map n ↦ 2P(n) + 1 cannot keep increasing for more than a bounded number of steps.
M: Prove there is $K$ such that no orbit of $n\mapsto 2P(n)+1$ has $K$ consecutive increases, and find the optimal $K$.

title: Sofa in three dimensions
W: Find the largest volume solid that can be carried around a right-angled corner in a square-cross-section hallway of width 1 in 3D.
M: Determine $\sup\{\mathrm{vol}(K)\}$ over compact $K\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ movable by rigid motions from one arm to the other of $L=([0,\infty)\times[0,1]\cup[0,1]\times[0,\infty))\times[0,1]$, and prove the maximiser is not a cylinder over a planar sofa.

title: Self-avoiding polygon on the hat tiling
W: Count self-avoiding walks along the edges of the hat tiling. Find the growth rate exactly.
M: Prove the connective constant $\mu$ of the hat-tiling edge graph exists (averaged over vertices) and determine it in closed form.

title: Unforced blow-up near the forced one
W: Show the known forced Navier–Stokes blow-up can be made to work with forcing that decays to zero at the blow-up time.
M: Prove there exist smooth $u_0$ and $f\in L^1_tL^2_x\cap C^\infty$ with $\|f(t)\|_{L^2}\to0$ as $t\to T^-$ such that the forced 3D NS solution blows up at $T$.

title: Prime-digit continued fractions in arithmetic progressions
W: Show there are infinitely many quadratic irrationals all of whose continued fraction digits are prime, in each real quadratic field.
M: Prove for every real quadratic field $K$ there are infinitely many $\alpha\in K$ with purely periodic continued fraction expansion having all partial quotients prime.

title: Hexagonal Lebesgue covering
W: Find the smallest convex shape that can cover every set of diameter 1, if covering is by translation only, not rotation.
M: Determine $\min\{\mathrm{area}(K):K$ convex, every set of diameter $1$ has a translate inside $K\}$, and prove the minimiser is unique.

title: Entropy of the Prime Nim word
W: Read the Grundy values of Prime Nim as an infinite word. Show the number of distinct length-N blocks grows exponentially and find the rate.
M: Prove $\lim_N\frac1N\log\#\{(G(n+1),\dots,G(n+N)):n\ge0\}$ exists and determine it.

title: Self-avoiding walk on the hat tiling scaling
W: Show long self-avoiding walks on the hat tiling spread out like distance n^{3/4}, the same as on the square grid.
M: Prove $\mathbb{E}|\omega_n|^2=n^{3/2+o(1)}$ for uniform $n$-step SAWs on the hat-tiling edge graph.

title: Largest-prime-factor random walk
W: Start at n and repeatedly move to n + P(n) or n − P(n) with a fair coin. Show this walk returns to small numbers with probability 1.
M: For the Markov chain $X_{t+1}=X_t\pm P(X_t)$ (fair signs, absorbed at $\le1$), prove absorption is almost sure from every start.

title: Ising with prime couplings
W: On the integer line, couple spins i and j with strength 1 if i − j is prime. Decide whether there is a phase transition.
M: For the 1D Ising model with $J_{ij}=\mathbf 1[|i-j|\in\mathbb{P}]\,|i-j|^{-2}$, prove a phase transition at finite $\beta_c$ and determine whether the magnetization jumps.

title: Random hat tilings
W: Choose a random tiling of a large hexagon by hats and their mirror images, with mirror images allowed freely. Find the entropy.
M: Prove tilings of regions by the hat and its reflection (both used freely) have positive entropy per tile, and compute it.

title: Stopping time law for P(n)+P(n+1)
W: For the map n ↦ P(n) + P(n+1), find the distribution of the number of steps to the {5, 8} loop.
M: Prove the stopping time $\sigma(n)$ of $f(n)=P(n)+P(n+1)$ satisfies $\sigma(n)/\log\log n\to c$ in density, and determine $c$.

title: Neighbour factors plus one
W: Map n to P(n − 1) + P(n + 1) + 1. Tested starts reach 8 → 11 → 9 or 10 → 15. Prove all do.
M: For $f(n)=P(n-1)+P(n+1)+1$, prove every orbit with $n\ge3$ reaches $(8,11,9)$ or $(10,15)$.

title: Minimal degree of a Jacobian counterexample
W: The first counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture in three dimensions has degree 7. Find the smallest possible degree.
M: Determine $\min\deg F$ over polynomial maps $F:\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ with $\det JF\equiv1$ and $F$ not injective.

title: Tileability by the spectre is undecidable for regions with holes
W: Show deciding whether a finite region with holes can be tiled by spectres is NP-complete.
M: Prove NP-completeness of: given a finite polygonal region $R$ (with holes), decide whether $R$ is tileable by copies of the spectre.

title: Sums of a square and a seven-free prime
W: Show almost every number is a square plus a prime with no 7 in its decimal digits.
M: Prove the set of $n$ not of the form $m^2+p$ with $p$ prime and $7\notin p$ has density zero.

title: Seven-free squares density
W: Count squares up to x with no 7 in their digits and find the exact power of x.
M: Prove $\#\{m\le\sqrt x:7\notin m^2\}=x^{\frac12\log_{10}9+o(1)}$.

title: Largest prime factor of n^n + 1
W: Show P(n^n + 1) / n tends to infinity.
M: Prove $P(n^n+1)/n\to\infty$.

title: Hadwiger number of square sums
W: Find the largest complete graph minor in the square-sum graph on 1 to N.
M: Determine the order of magnitude of $h(S_N)$, the largest $t$ with $K_t\preceq S_N$.
